context_requirements: No human cell line in this panel is known to express a direct target of HIV integrase inhibitors; the intended target (HIV integrase) is absent.
Any transcriptional response would require off-target engagement at 10 micromolar, which is not established for these drugs in these lineages.
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines.
Shared transcriptional signature across multiple lines that is absent in vehicle controls.
Evidence of RELA-dependent transcriptional changes at 10 micromolar.

evidence.supports: Raltegravir did not reduce HCV RNA in Huh7.5JFH1 hepatocytes, indicating no antiviral transcriptional response in a liver-derived line.
HIV integrase inhibitors inhibit herpesvirus replication only at submillimolar to micromolar concentrations via off-target viral proteins, not human host transcription.
Raltegravir acts on felid alphaherpesvirus 1 through viral DNA replication/late gene expression, not through a human transcriptional program.
Cabotegravir alters UGT enzyme expression and inflammatory cytokines in mouse liver and brain, suggesting possible off-target transcriptional effects at high exposure.

Dolutegravir derivatives, not dolutegravir itself, induce apoptosis in HepG2/Huh7 cells, indicating the parent HIV integrase inhibitor class lacks intrinsic antiproliferative transcriptional activity.
